result.summary: Manual review of 3 supplied files: src/shared/connection-manager/wire.ts, its unit test, and Kotlin ConnectionProtocol.kt. I found one concrete defect, and the review does not approve BUILD. The Kotlin public-config check uses java.net.URI to detect credentials embedded in an endpoint. For endpoints like `redis://:pw@my_host:6379`, java.net.URI silently drops the userinfo, so Kotlin accepts a safe read that the TypeScript decoder rejects. The rest of the TS/Kotlin decoder parity looks consistent, and I found no other defects there. The transport, session-owner and UI files that most of the assigned obligations depend on were not supplied, so those obligations are could-not-verify.

findings.trigger: A safe read or list reply from a daemon, or a draft public patch, carries `publicConfig.endpoint` such as `redis://:pw@my_host:6379` or `postgresql://u:p@a:1,b:2/db`. These have an underscore in the host or multiple hosts.
findings.defect: The credential-in-endpoint check uses `java.net.URI(...).rawUserInfo`. When the authority is not a valid server-based authority (underscore host, multi-host list), java.net.URI falls back to a registry-based authority. That fallback leaves `rawUserInfo` null and throws nothing, so the endpoint passes. The TS decoder uses WHATWG `new URL`, which sees the password (opaque host for non-special schemes) or throws on the invalid port, and refuses the row. Kotlin therefore accepts a safe read with an embedded credential that TS refuses. This breaks the shared strict privacy boundary and cross-language parity. The same java.net.URI strictness can also throw on endpoints WHATWG accepts, such as a space or `{` in the query. That turns one row into a whole-list read-error in Kotlin only.
findings.evidence: ConnectionProtocol.kt around line 217: `val uri = URI(child.asString); if (uri.scheme == null || uri.rawUserInfo != null) fail()`. wire.ts safePublicFields: `const url=new URL(child);if(url.username||url.password)fail();`. The line number is counted from the supplied diff and may be off by one or two. The corpus-based TS test covers only the single-host `postgresql://secret:password@fixture.invalid/db` case. No supplied Kotlin test covers underscore or multi-host userinfo. Java's fallback behavior comes from my knowledge of java.net.URI, not from supplied evidence.
findings.remedy: Do not rely on java.net.URI userinfo detection. Extract the authority textually: the segment after `scheme://` up to the first `/`, `?` or `#`. Fail if it contains `@`. Alternatively, reject any `@` in the authority before parsing. Add Kotlin fixtures for an underscore host with a password, multi-host with userinfo, and an endpoint with a space. Make the TS and Kotlin corpus assert identical outcomes for all of them.

obligations.evidence: ConnectionManagerState (sc7 model, dirty/draft/list-state transitions) is not in the supplied files. wire.ts and ConnectionProtocol.kt only supply strict decoders; read-error is a thrown fixed-message error with no empty-list fallback.

The TS and Kotlin decoders are otherwise exact and bounded, with fixed messages and no raw JSON editing. The Kotlin endpoint-credential check (ConnectionProtocol.kt ~217) is weaker than the TS check, so strict safe-read validation is not equivalent across clients (see finding). DaemonGatewayService and UnixSocketDaemonRpc.kt were not supplied.
The session owner, ipc-client.ts, extension.ts, ConnectionsSessionService.kt and the Kotlin persistent lane were not supplied. Only the decoders were.

No transport or recovery-effect code for written-unanswered state, freezing ticket+payload or same-ticket replay was supplied. Decoders do tie operationId, key and mode to the expectation, which helps replay matching.
ConnectionProtocol.kt adds no state to a gateway and is a separate object. DaemonGatewayService.kt itself was not supplied, so statelessness is not verifiable.
Workbench control-owner, delegated-lane and 90s lease code were not supplied.
New decoders are additive in new files. Preservation of the one-shot IpcClient and the Kotlin gateway cannot be confirmed without the transport diffs.

wire.ts copies data descriptors only (no accessors, prototypes, symbols, sparse or cyclic data) with byte, depth, node, string and item limits. It validates exact discriminated shapes, expected key/operation/epoch/mode, disables unknown descriptor schemas, and emits fixed error text. It imports no daemon runtime (the test imports the daemon, which is fine). The shared parsers in connection-management-wire.ts were not seen, and tests were not run.
No Kotlin persistent lane code or transport tests (UnixSocketDaemonRpc.kt) were supplied. ConnectionProtocol.requestData and parseData are only helper boundaries.
Kotlin Test/cancel wiring and EDT delivery were not supplied. Only the testResult decoder was.
No two-owner isolation implementation or tests were supplied.
Live lifecycle verification is out of scope of the supplied static files. Per the user, JetBrains live UI is deferred.

limitations: No tool calls were made, and no tests were run.

This batch is named transport-1, but the transport code was not supplied: src/shared/ipc-client.ts, UnixSocketDaemonRpc.kt, DaemonGatewayService.kt, ConnectionsSessionService.kt, extension.ts and InsrcProjectOpenActivity.kt.

The shared parsers in src/shared/connection-management-wire.ts (managementHandshake, parseDraftTestResult, parseOperationTicket) and the fixture corpus were not seen. TS-versus-Kotlin ticket, capability and test-result parity was therefore compared only structurally.
No Kotlin tests were supplied for ConnectionProtocol.kt.
The line number in the finding is counted by hand from the diff.
